newsitem.title: UK: Modern crude tanker tonnage thinner in Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Modern crude tanker tonnage thinner in Mideast.

text.p: Crude tanker charter rates in the all important Middle East Gulf nudged higher on Wednesday amid good fixing and thinning supplies of modern tonnage.
Other areas saw broadly steady rates, apart from a weakening Mediterranean market.

Shipping brokers said South Korean and Japanese charterers were dominating the market and that good quality VLCCs to Japan should secure W60, Singapore and South Korea W52.5-55, the U.S. Gulf W52.5 and UKC W52.5.
"There's quite a few 1970s VLCCs which charterers could probably knock down to W50 to Singapore," said one broker.
The sector looked firm, but any significant rise in rates would have to come from charterers getting caught short when looking for modern tonnage.

In the Mediterranean fixing was slow and the market looked weaker. "If we have another couple of poor days we will see rates go down to W90 (on 80,000 tonners going cross Med), said an Italian broker. Rates were currently around W100.
Interest in suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) has lessened and W70 will secure an older vessel and W80 for a modern ship, but rates were seen to have bottomed out.
The UKC sector saw a VLCC fixed at a lump sum of $1.1 million by Glencore to take Brent to South Africa. Rates on VLCCs transatlantic were unchanged around W62.5.
Rates for aframaxes going cross UKC were put around W102.5-105 amid plentiful supplies of tonnage an little potential for rate increases, brokers said.
In the Caribbean up U.S. coast market 70,000 tonners were assessed by brokers at W135-140.
